scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: Hello, this is the Office department (our PCs are on
192.168.3.x). All morning we haven't been able to reach the Internet Lab
computers (the 128.168.0.x machines) -- everything over there just times out
for us. Other things seem fine from here. Nobody in our office understands the
network side, I'm afraid. Could someone check what's wrong and fix it? Thank
you so much!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully healthy. The Office department's complaint that 192.168.3.x
hosts cannot reach 128.168.0.x Internet Lab machines is not reproducible and is
not supported by any evidence in the live lab.

Direct ICMP probes from every Office host (office_pc, enquiry, exam_cell, tpo)
to every Internet Lab host (pc2–pc5) succeed with 0% packet loss and consistent
~1–2 ms RTT, reflecting the expected two-router path via router1 and router2
(TTL arriving at 62 confirms exactly two L3 hops). The full lab-wide reachability
sweep corroborates this: every sampled pair achieves 0% loss in both directions.

The RIPv2 control plane is fully converged on all three routers: router2 directly
connects 128.168.0.0/16 and advertises it via the 20.0.0.0/8 WAN to router1,
which in turn propagates it to router0; the reverse path for 192.168.3.0/24 is
symmetric. No iptables/netfilter rules exist on any router — all FORWARD chains
are ACCEPT with no entries. All end-host IP addresses and default gateways are
correctly assigned (Office GW = 192.168.3.1, Internet-Lab GW = 128.168.0.1).

Root cause: there is no network fault. The reported symptom does not correspond
to any misconfiguration, routing deficiency, ACL, or data-plane failure present
in this topology.

Corrective action: No network changes are needed. The issue should be escalated
to the end users' workstations (host-side firewall, application-layer timeout
settings, or DNS resolution) rather than the network infrastructure.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup shows 0% loss ICMP from Office to 128.168.0.0/16 and describes RIPv2 convergence and propagation of the prefix across router2→router1→router0, indicating inter-router links are up and the prefix is reachable.

The agent's conclusion is fully supported by the investigation log: repeated successful ICMP tests, routing configs/routes, iptables output, host addressing, and a full reachability sweep are present and justify 'no network fault'. Inference steps follow logically and the essential checks were performed.
